identification.summary: Trend Micro tracks SHADOW-EARTH-053 as a temporary intrusion set (provisional cluster, not a formally attributed group) that it assesses to be aligned with China's broader strategic interests [S1]. It targets government entities and critical infrastructure in at least eight countries by exploiting unpatched internet-facing Microsoft Exchange and IIS servers, then deploying web shells and the ShadowPad backdoor [S1].
identification.firstObserved: Activity traced back to at least December 2024 per Trend Micro [S1]; disclosure dated 2026-04-30.
identification.notes: No Microsoft actor name is mapped to this cluster in the sources gathered. Trend Micro tracks a related intrusion set, SHADOW-EARTH-054; nearly half of victims were compromised by both,  but no evidence of direct operational coordination . Secondary reporting notes some network overlap with CL-STA-0049, Earth Alux and REF7707, and that other researchers link the attack chain to UNC6595; these are other vendors' clusters and are not merged here [S3]. Noodle RAT (Linux) and CVE-2025-55182 appear only as a weaker, case-specific association in press coverage [S3]. Trend Micro's primary page was only available through search-result summaries, not opened directly [S1].

attribution.confidence: Trend Micro describes the cluster as China-aligned and a temporary intrusion set pending formal attribution; it attributes the observed samples to the cluster with low confidence [S1]. No government attribution found.
attribution.basis: Trend Micro tooling and victimology (ShadowPad, widely associated with China-linked espionage) [S1].

objectives: Cyberespionage against government, defense and critical-infrastructure organizations, consistent with Trend Micro's assessment of alignment with China's strategic interests; mailbox content collection is indicated by the imported record and not confirmed in the sources I could open [S1].

targeting.notes: At least eight countries over roughly the past year per Trend Micro; Poland is the only European country in the footprint [S1][S3]. Journalist and activist targeting in some headlines belongs to separate Citizen Lab reporting (GLITTER CARP, SEQUIN CARP), not to this cluster [S3].

capabilities.summary: Initial access through known flaws in internet-facing Exchange (ProxyLogon family: CVE-2021-26855, CVE-2021-26857, CVE-2021-26858, CVE-2021-27065) and IIS servers, many on systems that should already have been patched [S3]. Post-exploitation includes GODZILLA web shells, credential theft (Mimikatz listed in one summary), tunneling and lateral-movement tools (IOX; GOST and Wstunnel in one summary), and ShadowPad loaded by DLL sideloading [S3].

ExchangeExport, WMIC lateral movement and the Noodle RAT / CVE-2025-55182 link appear in the imported record but could not be confirmed in sources I saw; Noodle RAT/React2Shell is a press-reported single-case association [S3].
C2 infrastructure and indicators are not captured.
Overlaps with CL-STA-0049, Earth Alux, REF7707, UNC6595 and SHADOW-EARTH-054 are unresolved [S3].
No government attribution; sponsor not established.
Specific victim organizations and data stolen are not public in the sources gathered.

Industrial Cyber, Cyber Security News, GrandLinux and Trend Micro Noodle RAT URLs were not seen in search results and were removed with claims resting only on them (IT/transport sectors, identical tool hashes, AnyDesk).

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Internet-facing Exchange and IIS servers at government, defense and transportation organizations, including partner nations in the Indo-Pacific and Poland, are key terrain. STEP 2: The actor relies on old, patched flaws, so unpatched legacy servers are the exploitable seam [S3]. STEP 3: Template is ProxyLogon-family exploit, GODZILLA web shell, credential theft, tunneling, then ShadowPad via DLL sideloading [S3]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued opportunistic exploitation of unpatched Exchange/IIS in Asian and NATO government and defense networks. MDCOA is use of established footholds in partner-nation defense networks for collection against regional operations. Candidate indicators: new ASPX web shells on Exchange/IIS, unsigned DLLs sideloaded by legitimate binaries, and unexpected tunneling tools [S3].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track patch status of Exchange and IIS across the DODIN and partner networks. (2) Authorities: partner-network remediation depends on host-nation and coalition agreements. (3) Mission assurance: prioritize mail and web servers supporting command communications. (4) Coordination: share indicators with DC3, DIB partners and allies, noting the cluster overlap with SHADOW-EARTH-054 .

provenance.importedSummary: SHADOW-EARTH-053 is a China-aligned threat group exploiting unpatched Microsoft Exchange Server vulnerabilities, specifically CVE-2021-26855, to conduct cyberespionage against government and defense-linked targets across Asia and Europe. The group primarily deploys ShadowPad malware, utilizing techniques such as credential dumping, tunneling tools, and lateral movement via WMIC. They have also been observed installing web shells for persistence and leveraging a custom ExchangeExport tool to extract high-value mailbox contents. Additionally, low-confidence associations with Noodle RAT and CVE-2025-55182 have been noted in their operations.
